title: Persian Female Warrior - Real-time Character
content:
## _Step into a real-time character creation journey inspired by Netflix's 'Jibaro'! Join character artist Juhwan Jeon as he explores new creative horizons by blending AI technology with traditional 3D pipelines._

# **![5912fa4bc7414448851f8afa3bca6baa](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/5912fa4bc7414448851f8afa3bca6baa1.jpg)Please introduce yourself briefly and tell us what inspired you to start 3D design.**

Hello. My name is Juhwan Jeon, and I am currently working as a character artist in the gaming industry.

I have loved animation and games since childhood, and was particularly fascinated by the process of realizing ultra-realistic graphics, which led me to pursue 3D design. This interest naturally guided me to major in a related field at university. Today, I specialize in creating game characters based on real-time rendering.

![f0d13d6dfece4d8791a9cca66cef1037](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/f0d13d6dfece4d8791a9cca66cef10372.jpg)

# **Could you tell us about the project you have recently worked on?**

For a recent personal project, I created a female warrior character with a Persian flair. I was deeply inspired by the character 'Jibaro' from the Netflix series Love, Death & Robots, especially the striking combination of ornate jewelry, intricate accessories, and an aesthetic that coexists as both beautiful and intimidating.

Drawing from this inspiration, my goal was to craft a character that embodies both elegance and strength. To experiment with new production workflows, I also integrated AI technology into certain stages of the process.

Rather than using AI as a direct asset generation tool, I utilized it to extract patterns for texturing and to recombine images to create novel design elements. I also leveraged AI during the initial modeling of the figure base to rapidly materialize my ideas.

Personally, I view AI not as a technology to replace artists, but as a supportive tool to enhance workflow efficiency and explore new creative possibilities. I plan to continue experimenting with it in various ways moving forward.

# **![bc236f8d6fc94989b551025a47d34c4d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/bc236f8d6fc94989b551025a47d34c4d3.jpg)![94c768b128de4615a1fa391333aae83f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/94c768b128de4615a1fa391333aae83f2_1.jpg)![ce463ecd34da459197af7bba6a33425d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/ce463ecd34da459197af7bba6a33425d2_2.jpg)Could you provide a brief overview of the various tools used in your pipeline?**

For this project, I crafted the hard-surface elements using 3ds Max, and designed the garments utilizing Marvelous Designer and ZBrush. Texturing was completed in Substance 3D Painter, and the final rendering was executed in Unreal Engine 5.

For the garment creation, as I lacked specialized fashion design knowledge, I began with the simplest possible shapes and utilized Marvelous Designer only where necessary. I believe there is a limit to expressing natural wrinkles solely through manual work. Therefore, I first established the overall silhouette and major folds in Marvelous Designer, and then refined the detailed wrinkles using ZBrush's Dynamics feature along with additional sculpting.

![3b09607c951b455e8403c034a7704155](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/3b09607c951b455e8403c034a77041554.png)![159d6fe8124c4c5eaf0280704cb309f7](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/159d6fe8124c4c5eaf0280704cb309f75.jpg)![28439212fa2242aea18ed4eaff1083df](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/28439212fa2242aea18ed4eaff1083df3_1.png)

# **Every project comes with its own highlights and challenges. What was the most enjoyable part of the process for you, and what did you find the most challenging?**

A: My favorite part of the workflow is crafting realistic, hard-surface-based accessories. I also thoroughly enjoy the texturing process, where I can express different material finishes and wear-and-tear to breathe life and realism into a character. Seeing these meticulous details accumulate to complete a single character brings me a profound sense of accomplishment and joy as a character artist.

Conversely, the most challenging aspect was applying in-engine simulations to give the finished character a more natural and dynamic sense of life. Managing a multitude of features and settings simultaneously during the rendering stage felt quite complex, but through a process of trial and error, I was able to get closer to my desired outcome.

# **![e5e800ee415549cdac1ddfb94ecde38b](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/e5e800ee415549cdac1ddfb94ecde38b6.jpg)![9ec2196a3c944dc0a5165eb114f34a61](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/9ec2196a3c944dc0a5165eb114f34a617.jpg)**

# **Lastly, do you have any advice for those who are just starting out in 3D art? This could be career advice, the mindset needed when creating artwork, or anything else you'd like to share.**

A: Since I am not someone with extraordinary natural talent—much like most people—I believe that consistency and patience are far more critical to becoming a great character artist. As you work, you will inevitably face countless trials and errors, but I believe the experiences gained through that process are what ultimately translate into true skill.

Additionally, keeping an open mind toward new tools and technologies is essential. Recently, new technologies, including AI, are emerging at a rapid pace, and actual production workflows are constantly evolving. I, too, am continuously learning to ensure I do not fall behind, and I believe the ability to adapt to these changes will only become increasingly important in the future.

![f523f007ac9140149509629f0192aff4](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/690f48f7cb784e2688451fe60488dbc2/images/f523f007ac9140149509629f0192aff48.jpg)

title: Where Imagination Takes Shape: 3DCG Artist Kota Yamaji on Cloth Simulation and Digital Fashion with Marvelous Designer
content:
## ![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/c5ef7aca4a594b75a49b2df9d0342e72Header_thumb%20%281%29.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/9f8259e036ed40dfa0914cb97af4de81Header_thumb.png)_Kota Yamaji is a 3DCG artist and illustrator whose work lives at the intersection of fashion and visual arts. Once a graduate of Tama Art University's Department of Graphic Design, and currently a lecturer, he builds boldly colored figures whose garments feel both impossible and convincingly real._

  
Working with Marvelous Designer, Cinema 4D, and ZBrush, Kota uses cloth simulation to chase a kind of realism that pure sculpting can't easily reach.   
Drawing on his portfolio "[Digital Fashion Project](https://kotayamaji.com/digitalfashion.html)," we talk with him about his encounters with digital art and Marvelous Designer, where his ideas come from, and how he thinks about the future of digital fashion.

# **  
![96fae3fb8e9a4684b345ea6a7c9b28c6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/96fae3fb8e9a4684b345ea6a7c9b28c6190124.jpg)  
Meet the artist**

**First, please introduce yourself to the community.**

My name is Kota Yamaji. After graduating from the Department of Graphic Design at Tama Art University, I began creating illustration and moving-image work using 3DCG. I currently also teach 3DCG as a part-time lecturer at Tama Art University.  


**Tell us how you got into art and creation, and how you came to teach CG at Tama Art University. How do you see the potential of 3DCG within art?**

  
Since I went to an art university to begin with, if you think of "creation" in the broadest sense, my first real starting point was probably preparing for the art school entrance exams. But when it comes to digital art specifically, the trigger was learning 3DCG software during my university years.   
  
3DCG isn't limited to digital media—it can be applied physically as well, through things like 3D printing, so I think there are all kinds of ways to make use of it. As for how I ended up teaching, a professor from my student days suddenly got in touch with me. It seems they had seen my work somewhere.

![5ce6e7bb6bca4ded885502190b15d6d8](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/5ce6e7bb6bca4ded885502190b15d6d8181109.jpg)

* * *

# **Discovering Marvelous Designer**

**What first led you to start using Marvelous Designer? Can you tell us about the moment you felt, "This is something I can use for my own work"?**

What got me started was seeing the WIP (work-in-progress) posts of an artist I admire and noticing that Marvelous Designer was part of their workflow.

  
**In a pipeline that combines Cinema 4D and ZBrush, at what point do you reach for Marvelous Designer? Where do you feel it does something the other tools simply can't replace?**

I mostly use it to create clothing for characters. Realistic garment expression really is something only simulation can deliver. With sculpt modeling in ZBrush and similar tools, it might be possible to build something realistic if you put in enough time—but the sheer ease of simulation is a genuine draw.

![d1ae1914436d4952b3211e9733c28727](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/d1ae1914436d4952b3211e9733c28727Screenshot%202026-06-11%20060631.png)_Yamaji's Marvelous Designer workspace—patterning in the 2D window with the garment draped on the avatar in 3D._

![4e4c17b0fbad461f87845b57a3db7474](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/4e4c17b0fbad461f87845b57a3db7474Screenshot%202026-06-11%20061035.png)_Draping done in Marvelous Designer_  


![026e811d736946598ce86eceedec7819](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/026e811d736946598ce86eceedec7819250305.png)

![33e71792ebec4f2cbbf371c4d939f76d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/33e71792ebec4f2cbbf371c4d939f76d250305_posed.png)  
 _A garment simulated on the avatar (first) and carried through to a dynamic pose (second), with texturing also handled in Marvelous Designer._

  
![c7fc30501efa4a0abd47ee0020d3cb14](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/c7fc30501efa4a0abd47ee0020d3cb14Screenshot%202026-06-11%20061638.png)_Working on Cinema 4D_

![a3e191350afc4c1c8c7edf0089db5627](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/a3e191350afc4c1c8c7edf0089db5627250305.jpg) _Final Visual_

* * *

# **Ideas and Inspiration**

**Where do your ideas usually come from? Music, fashion, everyday scenery—what tends to be the starting point for your work?**

I'm influenced by so many different things that it's hard to narrow it down to any single one. I get the sense that my final inspiration comes from an abstracted, almost unspeakable space where all of those things mix together.

**When you make digital clothing, are you conscious of the physical constraints of real garments—gravity, material, stitching? Or do you enjoy deliberately freeing yourself from those constraints?**

When making something digital, I think it often becomes more interesting if you ignore those constraints. But at the same time, simulation is exactly what makes realistic expression possible through physical constraints—so I feel it's something of a trade-off.

  
![e0d5f6519e064aa59dddbacd92ae0219](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/e0d5f6519e064aa59dddbacd92ae0219190129.jpg)

* * *

# **The Future of Digital Fashion**

**When it comes to the possibilities of digital fashion, what kind of future do you picture for yourself?**

I don't have all that much specialized knowledge myself, but I think it would be exciting if digital fashion came to be used more often in the creation of real garments.   
  
I'm curious about what kind of technical progress might emerge on the efficiency side—things like the extensibility of materials, or cutting out the labor of physically cutting fabric. And if individual designers could easily output the clothing they make digitally into the real world, I think that would be even more interesting.

  
![71c12cd91f10443a85d493385d00f641](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/71c12cd91f10443a85d493385d00f641Screenshot%202026-06-11%20061827.png)_Footwear created using Marvelous Designer_

  
![85661c9daeb84e75903fbfba22789340](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/85661c9daeb84e75903fbfba22789340shoes02.png)

![3cee1bc68034426d887edc43963f92ed](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/95da5a77501a4e86b1ab94ffa8de3287/images/3cee1bc68034426d887edc43963f92ed250308.jpg) _Final Visual_

* * *

 _A warm thank you to Kota Yamaji for sharing his process with the community!_  
_Follow Kota's socials to experience more of the vivid world of 3DCG and digital fashion that he creates._

  * Kota Yamaji — [Digital Fashion Project](https://kotayamaji.com/digitalfashion.html)

  * Instagram: [@kotayamaji](https://www.instagram.com/kotayamaji)

  * X: [@k0tayamaji](https://x.com/k0tayamaji)

  * Behance: [Kota Yamaji](https://www.behance.net/kotayamaji)
content_description: Showcasing 3DCG artist Kota Yamaji’s innovative blend of fashion and digital art through his use of Marvelous Designer, Cinema 4D, and ZBrush to create realistic and imaginative digital garments.

title: 【6/23 イベント】Marvelous Designer 新機能紹介ウェビナーが開催されます！
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/c4346de9eedb4b3a878a79e293a2a0be/images/ca50ffbe86be4ea2a4a6e5a460719154273_seminar_md_top.jpg)![e352646725a44cbba6c9f867ff18e8b3](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/c4346de9eedb4b3a878a79e293a2a0be/images/e352646725a44cbba6c9f867ff18e8b3273_seminar_md_full.jpg)

この度、[株式会社ボーンデジタル主催のウェビナー](https://www.borndigital.co.jp/seminar/marvelous-designer_update_2026_0623/)に、Marvelous Designerがゲストとして参加します！**  
**今回は、特別企画として、Marvelous Designerの開発を行っているソウル本社の開発チームがオンラインで登壇する特別企画つきです。  
日本のユーザーとMarvelous Designerの開発陣を、生放送で直接つなげる初めての試みを実現いたしました。

## なぜ今回、韓国の開発チームが日本のイベントに？

日本のゲーム、アニメーション / 映像表現における盛り上がりは、韓国の開発陣もかなり注目しています。 3DCGの現場でMarvelous Designerがどう使われているのか、どんな機能が求められているのか？  
その関心の高さが、今回のウェビナー参加につながりました。

最新のバージョンでは、これまで日本や世界各地のユーザーからいただいた要望や機能リクエストをひとつでも多く反映すべく、変更を加えております。  
まだMarvelous Designerを使ったことがない方も、以前さわったことがある方も、きっと「ここまで変わったの！？」と驚いていただけるアップデートになっています。

今回のイベントでは、ゲーム、アニメーション、映像におけるクリエイターにぜひお役立ていただけそうな機能をピックアップしました。  
2024〜2026年のアップデートの中から、実務にてMarvelous Designer を使っている / 使いたいクリエイターの方に、「これは役に立つ！」と思っていただける新機能を厳選してご紹介いたします。

## 当日のプログラム

**① 新機能デモンストレーション**   
2024年から2026年までの中から、特におすすめの機能をMarvelous Designerの日本チームが紹介いたします。

**② 開発背景トーク（ 韓国開発チーム登壇 ）**   
どんなメンバーで開発しているのか？ユーザーの声をどう集めているのか？ユーザーの要望から生まれた機能とは？  
Marvelous Designerの開発の裏側をご紹介いたします。

**③ ライブQ &Aセッション**   
参加者からの質問に開発者がその場で回答。**どんな質問でも大歓迎です！**   
事前質問も募集していますが、当日の質問もチャットにて受け付けます。  
通訳が同席するので、ご質問は日本語でOKです。

## ピックアップする新機能（一部）

**2Dパターン変形時の3D形状保持（2026）**

![a812fea058d54c7f95df7c8ed765aae6](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/c4346de9eedb4b3a878a79e293a2a0be/images/a812fea058d54c7f95df7c8ed765aae603%20Preserve%203D%20Garment%20Shape%20on%202D%20Scaling.png)

3D衣服の形状を保ったまま、2Dパターンのサイズを変更できます

**選択のみ表示（2026）**

![553b6e2b0cbe47209ab19b4faad676bf](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/c4346de9eedb4b3a878a79e293a2a0be/images/553b6e2b0cbe47209ab19b4faad676bf18%20Isolate%20Selection.png)

選択した3Dオブジェクトだけを表示でき、複雑なシーンでも作業に集中できます

**3Dペンシル（2026）**

![c73e0c73c88445ddae719349572aaf9f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/c4346de9eedb4b3a878a79e293a2a0be/images/c73e0c73c88445ddae719349572aaf9f02%203D%20Pencil.png)

3Dアバター上にラインを描くだけで2Dパターンを自動生成し、衣服を制作できます

**四角ポリゴンリメッシュの改善（2025）**

![a8deeda29cc441cb99339aae00f4602e](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/c4346de9eedb4b3a878a79e293a2a0be/images/a8deeda29cc441cb99339aae00f4602eQuad_Improvement.png)

メッシュ品質が大幅に向上、エッジラインの作成がより速く美しく

**側面・裏面のUV拡張（2025）**

![98d7a204ab414017ade83716c4210909](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/c4346de9eedb4b3a878a79e293a2a0be/images/98d7a204ab414017ade83716c4210909Side_and_back_UV_expansion.png)

前面だけでなく側面・裏面もUV展開可能に

**GPUシミュレーションの改善（2024〜）**

![feb3e33e263c4daa856758ef085a8dfd](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/c4346de9eedb4b3a878a79e293a2a0be/images/feb3e33e263c4daa856758ef085a8dfd1_GPU_Simulation_Improvements.webp)

CPUと同等の衝突処理精度を維持。  
バージョン2026.0では副資材のGPUシミュレーションにも対応しました

* * *

## こんな方におすすめ

ゲーム・アニメ業界の3Dキャラクターアーティスト、CG衣装のクリエイター・モデラー、企業所属のモデラーの方のご参加をおすすめします。  
また、「開発チームに直接質問してみたい」「最近のアップデートを知りたい」「これからMarvelous Designerを使ってみたい」という方にもぴったりのウェビナーです。

* * *

## 開催概要

> **開催日** 2026年6月23日(火)  
> **時間** 13:00〜14:30  
> **会場** オンライン  
> **参加費** 無料 ※事前登録必須  
>   
> **主催** 株式会社ボーンデジタル  
> **協力** CLO Virtual Fashion Inc.

ゲストとして、CLO Virtual Fashion Inc. CTOのSean Jeon、そしてMarvelous DesignerプロダクトマネージャーのAina Chungが登壇を予定しております。

* * *

## ご登録はお早めに！

本ウェビナーは**事前登録制** です。

title: Recreating the Richness of Traditional Indian Costume with Marvelous Designer
content:
![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/72aaae299f0a41c6b102f152cadf78a1/images/366fb9bc4626458f90c96f15be45e2a7Header_EN%20%282%29.png)![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/72aaae299f0a41c6b102f152cadf78a1/images/53157150cf9a411784e7784baa7c8025Header_EN%20%281%29.png)Meet [**Vaibhav Negi**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/vaibhavnegi/), a CGI industry veteran with 10+ years of experience and a member of Marvelous Designer. In this spotlight, Vaibhav shares how he brought a photoreal character inspired by India’s traditional ritual, Bhoota Kola, to life. Discover how he utilized Marvelous Designer for over 80% of the asset—from complex layered garments to a brilliant workaround for creating intricate flower garlands and straw skirts using lightweight, production-ready workflows.

* * *

  
![743e4fbec1164392aa187b0bf6376344](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/72aaae299f0a41c6b102f152cadf78a1/images/743e4fbec1164392aa187b0bf63763443%20%281%29.jpg)

# **Software Used**

Blender – lighting, texturing, Rendering  
Marvelous Designer – Cloth Simulation & Animation

# **Artist Introduction**

Hey, I’m Vaibhav. I feel like an imposter here because I’m part of Marvelous Designer’s internal design team. That said, long before I joined the company, I was already a strong believer in the software.

I have over 10 years of experience in CGI, with more than six years of that spent using Marvelous Designer as a core part of my workflow. My background is in CGI advertising and automotive visualization, while my personal passion lies in creating animated short films and video games.

Throughout my career, Marvelous Designer has consistently been one of the tools that has had the biggest impact on both the quality and speed of my work.

# **Please introduce your project.**

The project I’ll be talking about today is a character inspired by Bhoota Kola, one of India’s many traditional ritual practices. The ritual also served as the central theme of the critically acclaimed Indian film Kantara.

My goal was to create a photoreal digital replica of the performer that could be optimized for both film and game production. More than 80% of the asset was created using Marvelous Designer.  
![a7395529dafb48e0b29e2e52b281d55c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/72aaae299f0a41c6b102f152cadf78a1/images/a7395529dafb48e0b29e2e52b281d55cArtboard%201.jpg)![ab88e7776b2c4c86884460108bf9c3c9](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/72aaae299f0a41c6b102f152cadf78a1/images/ab88e7776b2c4c86884460108bf9c3c9Screenshot%202026-05-28%20090507.png)The project also gave me an opportunity to explore complex layered garments and traditional ornaments, including flower garlands, ceremonial necklaces, and the iconic straw skirt. Beyond recreating the visual appearance, I wanted to capture the richness and authenticity of the costume while maintaining production-ready efficiency.

# **Tell us how Marvelous Designer creates value in this project.**

Character creation is a highly complex process. Sculpting every element by hand requires significant time, technical skill, and a deep understanding of form design. Realistic garments add another layer of complexity, and once the assets are created, they still need to be retopologized and UV-mapped before they become practical for film or game production.

For me, Marvelous Designer replaces much of the highly skilled craftsmanship involved in creating dimensional forms with the more structured and intuitive principles of garment design. That shift alone dramatically accelerates the process.![dddd4953699b4e42a4a602bf6b942e9f](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/72aaae299f0a41c6b102f152cadf78a1/images/dddd4953699b4e42a4a602bf6b942e9fArtboard%202.jpg)This project involved a large number of layered garments, and Marvelous Designer handled them exceptionally well. It remains the most natural and lifelike way I know of creating digital clothing.

The integrated retopology and UV workflow saved a tremendous amount of time and allowed me to add levels of detail that would have been difficult to achieve otherwise.

I also wanted to experiment with creating traditional flower garlands inside Marvelous Designer. The solution I arrived at was surprisingly simple but extremely effective. I created a tileable 3D pattern and used it as a button asset without enabling button simulation. This produced a visually rich garland that remained lightweight and efficient.

The straw skirt followed a similar philosophy. While it appears highly detailed, it was built from a single simulated strand setup that was duplicated and arranged repeatedly. The result was a complex-looking asset created through a very efficient workflow.

# **Are there any other unique projects you worked on using Marvelous Designer that you would like to showcase to our community?**

YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3IYeUIfTwEs?si=yk9M6jO1SaG4_sCg

Over the last few years, I’ve created several animated short films that relied heavily on Marvelous Designer, and I’m particularly proud of two projects.

The first,[____A House of My Own__](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3IYeUIfTwEs), is a personal tribute to one of my former rented apartments, the first place that truly felt like home.

The second is an adaptation of a story by one of my favorite writers, Ruskin Bond. Called [_In the dark_](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j14YXtGmwbw), The film was well received at several film events and earned multiple screenings, which was incredibly rewarding as an independent creator.  


YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j14YXtGmwbw?start=0

Both projects reinforced how valuable Marvelous Designer can be, not only for character work but also for storytelling.

# **What is your favorite feature or tool to use in Marvelous Designer?**

The **Retopology** and **UV Mapping** tools are an easy choice for me.

They make the transition from high-resolution assets to production-ready meshes incredibly intuitive. Being able to handle retopology and UVs directly within the same workflow saves time, reduces friction, and makes transferring detail from high-poly meshes much more efficient.

# **For other users considering Marvelous Designer, do you have any advice or experience to share?**

Two tips completely changed the way I work:

**Think in layers.** Approach your garments the same way you would approach a traditional painting. Focus on the large forms first, then gradually build detail. As sections are completed, freeze them and continue refining the next layer. This keeps simulations stable and the workflow manageable.

**Use cloth simulation, even if it’s subtle.** If you’re creating animated films, adding even a simple cloth simulation can bring a surprising amount of life and realism to a character. As a bonus, natural cloth movement can often help mask small imperfections in animation.

content_description: Discover how CGI artist Vaibhav Negi expertly uses Marvelous Designer to create photorealistic, production-ready digital characters inspired by traditional Indian rituals through innovative garment simulation and efficient workflows.

title: 안에 충전재가 비치는 다이렉트 다운공법으로 제작된 패딩 구현
content:
I would like to create a down jacket with a Direct Down construction, where the insulation is subtly visible through the outer fabric.

So far, I have tried building the garment using three separate layers: an outer shell, insulation, and lining. However, the result looks more like a foggy or hazy translucent material rather than the characteristic appearance of a Direct Down jacket. The ripstop texture, puckering gradients, and other fabric details also lose clarity because the opacity affects everything uniformly.

I have a few questions:

  1. Would it be better to incorporate the appearance of the insulation directly into the Base Color map, rather than relying on actual transparency?

  2. For the puckering around the quilted or stitched areas, would it be effective to create grayscale PNG masks and use them as Height, Normal, or displacement information to generate soft gradients?




These are the two approaches I am currently considering.

I would also like to know if there are any other methods that could achieve this effect more accurately. I'm open to using other software such as Substance 3D Designer, Substance Painter, Blender, Cinema 4D, Houdini, or any other tools if they provide a better solution.

My goal is to recreate the distinctive appearance seen in garments such as C.P. Company D.D. Shell pieces, where:

  * The ripstop texture remains clearly visible.

  * The insulation appears subtly visible beneath the fabric.

  * The puckering and quilting gradients are preserved.

  * The material does not simply look transparent or foggy.




What techniques, workflows, shaders, texture setups, or material construction methods would you recommend for achieving this effect as realistically as possible?

이렇게 안에 충전재가 비치는 다이렉트 다운공법으로 제작된 패딩을 제작하고싶습니다. 제가 시도 해보았던 방법은 "3개의 레이어로 각각 겉감/충전재/안감으로 구현을 하고자하니 뿌옇게 안개가 낀 느낌이고 퍼커링의 그라데이션 표현이나 립스탑 텍스쳐 표현도 같이 오퍼시티가 내려갑니다. 특유의 비친듯한 표현이 잘 안됩니다. " 제 질문은 1. 베이스 컬러맵 자체를 안의 충전재가 들어있는 듯한 느낌으로 가야할까요? 2. 퍼커링은 탑스티치를 png로 활용해서 그라데이션을 주는 방법으로 가야할까요? 제가 생각해본 방법은 이렇게 두가지인데 다른 방법들이 있다면 어떤 방법들이 있는지 전부 알고싶습니다. 타 소프트웨어를 활용하는 방법도 괜찮으니 구현가능한 방법에는 어떤것들이 있는지 알고싶습니다.![b7f97fb8f53542d8bf8587cb45821286](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202606/deb699946b1b4154a4b409d01749c5fb/images/b7f97fb8f53542d8bf8587cb45821286a_52dcd4eccfb7497cbbfb2cc730f758b4.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: perfect

Comment 2: Hi! First of all, thank you so much for the detailed outline of what you are trying to achieve. I also immediately thought to try with an edited Base Color Map (point 1). As for point 2, I do not know a use case, but it is worth a try and sounds reasonably likely to work, why not? Are you using the Fill tool or working with the Pressure function right now?
Reply 1: Hello! Thank you for your reply. I am using the pressure function to implement the wrinkles on the padding. I am not yet familiar with the filling function, so I don't find myself using it much. When I proceed with method #2, the swatch map itself does not produce the texture of actual filling that I expected; instead, it appears patchy.
content_description: This web page explores advanced material and texture techniques to realistically recreate the subtle insulation visibility, ripstop texture clarity, and quilted puckering effects characteristic of Direct Down construction in down jackets.
